scope: One under-reset connection to read the current NUCLEO-WB55RG application twice, reset once, and machine-check normal application resumption without any application or panel write command.

help_relevant_verbatim: Reset mode with UR connection mode is HWrst
-u,     --upload       : Upload the device memory content to a .bin/.hex/.srec/.s19 file
<address>          : Start address of read and upload
<size>             : Size of memory content to be read

prior_restore_programmer_stdout.observed: Under Reset, Hardware reset, Device ID 0x495, STM32WB5x/35xx, Cortex-M4, 3.24V, download verified

PROVEN: COMP-REQ-259 made one HOTPLUG upload attempt, obtained no bytes and ended NO_GO with zero candidate, restore or panel writes; HOTPLUG may not be retried here.
The installed STM32CubeProgrammer v2.22.0 help exposes UR, HWrst, upload address/size/file arguments and system reset as separate CLI operations.
The existing flash runner uses the exact connection prefix port=SWD mode=UR reset=HWrst freq=4000.
A prior restore on the same ST-LINK serial 066EFF535570514867221931 connected Under Reset at 3.24V and identified Device ID 0x495 / STM32WB5x/35xx / Cortex-M4 before verified programming.
The linker assigns application FLASH 0x08000000..0x0807FFFF, exactly 0x80000 bytes.
Historical normal-restore serial evidence contains both the Companion NUCLEO-WB55RG boot identity and the production BLE path ready marker.
Under-reset necessarily resets or holds the MCU during connection; the final -rst restarts the existing application, which may execute its existing display behavior.
INFERENCE: STM32CubeProgrammer's command sequencing accepts two upload operations followed by one reset in one process; if the installed version rejects that sequence, the single run must fail without splitting it into another connection.
Two byte-identical, full-length, nontrivial uploads with a plausible vector table and programmed span are sufficient to establish a reusable raw application-byte baseline.

The two historical boot markers within the bounded post-reset capture, with no diagnostic/error markers, are sufficient evidence that the pre-existing normal application resumed; they do not prove every peripheral or display behavior.
UNKNOWN: The current board application's raw SHA-256, vector words, programmed span and relation to the lost E199 Intel HEX file remain unknown before the admitted reads.
Whether the current application will emit both normal markers within the bounded serial window is unknown.
Physical screen appearance during the reset and resumed normal firmware is not observed or accepted in this Goal.
Option bytes, wireless stack, OTP, secrets, memory above 0x0807FFFF and SSD1681 controller state remain unread.
RISK: Under-reset disrupts normal MCU execution and the explicit reset restarts it; the existing application may refresh or otherwise change the display even though this runner sends no panel command.
An upload failure after the single connection begins cannot be retried or replaced by HOTPLUG, NORMAL, POWERDOWN, another reset or a second programmer process.
Short, long, inconsistent, all-zero/all-FF, implausible-vector or implausibly sparse data must be rejected and never used as a restore baseline.
A valid backup without normal boot evidence means application resumption is unproven and requires human attention without another reset or connection.

ADMISSION.serial_order: Open normal serial capture and receive its ready signal before launching the sole programmer process.
ADMISSION.backup_pass: two private 524288-byte identical files, common SHA-256, nonzero/non-FF, valid MSP/reset vector, first non-FF byte in the vector table and at least 4096-byte non-FF span with at least 1024 non-FF bytes
ADMISSION.normal_resume_pass: within at most 30 seconds after the reset, normal boot identity and production ready marker present; no readonly controller diagnostic, panel error or hardfault marker

non_goals: Write, erase, download, verify-write, read-unprotect, option-byte, wireless-stack or OTP operation
HOTPLUG, NORMAL, POWERDOWN, a second connection, retry, halt, run or hardRst command
Controller candidate, SSD1681 0x2D/0x2F or any 0x20/0x22/0x24/0x26/0x32/0x37 operation
Screen, residue, White/Black, rail, temperature, animation, touch, BLE, waveform, production or visual acceptance
Claim that the captured raw binary reproduces the lost E199 Intel HEX file
